articles.title: Dolly Parton: The life of an iconic country singer
articles.summary: Iconic country musician Dolly Parton has died at the age of 80, the singer's team announced on social media.
articles.body:
Iconic country musician Dolly Parton has died at the age of 80, her family announced on her social media.

"Sadness lies with us, not with Dolly," Parton's nephew Brian Seaver said in a video announcement.

In a seven-decade career, Parton won 10 Grammy awards, sold more than 100 million records worldwide, and wrote in excess of 3,000 songs.

Parton took her writing seriously, and considered herself a songwriter over everything else. "It's my way of expressing myself," she said. "It's my therapy."

She was also a savvy businesswoman who wasn't afraid to make tough decisions. Armed with a quick wit and southern charm, she took control of her show business career that spanned more than 60 years.

articles.title: Misoginia organizada: o conceito por trás do 'ranking' sexual em SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Especialistas falam sobre as hostilidades dirigidas às mulheres e as possibilidades de responsabilização dos suspeitos após a investigação da Delegacia de Defesa da Mulher (DDM) de Presidente Prudente (SP).
articles.summary: Em Presidente Prudente (SP), alunas de uma universidade privada foram expostas e avaliadas em um “ranking” sexual, compartilhado em um grupo fechado de um aplicativo de mensagens.
articles.body:
Polícia Civil investiga suposto ranking sexual com fotos de estudantes de universidade em Presidente Prudente (SP) — Foto: Redes Sociais/Reprodução

O dicionário explica a palavra “misoginia” como antipatia ou aversão mórbida às mulheres. Mas, na vida real, esse conceito é muito mais do que um verbete e alimenta a desigualdade, a violência e os discursos de ódio.

Em Presidente Prudente (SP), alunas de uma universidade privada foram expostas e avaliadas em um “ranking” sexual, compartilhado em um grupo fechado de um aplicativo de mensagens. O conteúdo foi vazado e expôs mensagens de teor sexual e depreciativo, gerando uma investigação da Polícia Civil, que havia recebido 10 denúncias de vítimas até esta terça-feira (25).

O caso provocou protestos com faixas e cartazes em frente à universidade, localizada às margens da Rodovia Raposo Tavares (SP-270). O coletivo “Frente pela Vida das Mulheres” emitiu uma nota de repúdio ao episódio, classificado como “ um ato de misoginia organizada ”.

A psicóloga e professora Viviane Melo de Mendonça, coordenadora do Núcleo de Estudos de Gênero, Diferenças e Sexualidades (NEGDS) da Universidade Federal de São Carlos (UFSCar), campus Sorocaba , concorda com a definição, esclarecendo que a palavra “organizada” não está sendo utilizada no sentido jurídico.

“O termo descreve uma prática coletiva, planejada e sistematizada. Não foi apenas um comentário individual, isolado. Houve apropriação de fotografias das estudantes, construção de critérios para classificá-las, produção de um ranking e circulação em um grupo específico. Criou-se coletivamente um instrumento para transformar mulheres em corpos avaliáveis e sexualmente disponíveis ao julgamento masculino”, explica.

A psicóloga esclarece que o caso é um exemplo de misoginia por tirar das mulheres a condição de pessoas, transformando-as em “objetos de consumo e comparação”. “Também é organizada por envolver um método, uma participação coletiva e validação daqueles que participam do grupo”.

No grupo onde o conteúdo foi compartilhado, os integrantes faziam diversos comentários sobre a lista. Em um deles, um dos alunos diz: “Tirei as lésbicas e as gordas”. Para Viviane, essa frase apresenta outra camada sobre o episódio.

“Isso confirma que essa violência não atingia todas as mulheres da mesma maneira. Combina misoginia, lesbofobia e gordofobia”, diz a psicóloga.

A psicóloga e professora Viviane Melo de Mendonça concorda com a definição de "misoginia organizada" para explicar o episódio — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal/Divulgação

Os conceitos de misoginia e machismo estão relacionados, mas Viviane destaca que são diferentes. Nas definições apresentadas pela psicóloga:

Misoginia - desprezo, aversão ou hostilidade dirigida às mulheres pelo fato de serem mulheres.

Machismo - sistema de ideias, valores e práticas que atribui aos homens uma posição de superioridade e distribui de maneira desigual o poder, a autoridade e a liberdade entre homens e mulheres.

“A misoginia é uma das formas pelas quais essa ordem machista é protegida e colocada em funcionamento. Ela aparece, principalmente, quando as mulheres são hostilizadas, humilhadas e punidas por não ocuparem o lugar que se espera delas. O machismo estabelece uma hierarquia entre homens e mulheres, enquanto a misoginia atua para punir e vigiar as mulheres dentro dessa hierarquia”, esclarece.

A psicóloga pontua, ainda, que a misoginia não aparece apenas quando alguém declara ódio explícito às mulheres. “Ela se manifesta em práticas de humilhação, objetificação, controle, intimidação e violência”.

Seja em redes sociais, plataformas de vídeos ou aplicativos de mensagens, a misoginia tem ganhado espaço e coro na internet. Para a psicóloga e coordenadora do NEGDS da UFSCar, o ambiente virtual produz uma sensação de segurança e impunidade aos agressores.

“As plataformas oferecem rapidez, grande alcance e a possibilidade de repetição, então, quando há uma fotografia ou uma ofensa, elas podem ser copiadas e compartilhadas inúmeras vezes e o dano continua mesmo depois que o conteúdo original é apagado. Isso é muito sério”, complementa.

Essa possibilidade de repetição, segundo Viviane, vai radicalizando a violência contra as mulheres. “Os algoritmos agravam o problema, pois conteúdos que provocam indignação e medo costumam gerar muito engajamento. Portanto, a misoginia que já existe na sociedade encontra, no ambiente digital, modos mais eficientes de organização, amplificação e permanência”.

É justamente na internet que percebemos o crescimento do movimento conhecido como “ red pill ”, que propaga teorias e preconceitos direcionados às mulheres. A psicóloga analisa que esses discursos dizem aos homens, especialmente aos mais jovens, que a culpa pelas frustrações amorosas, profissionais e sexuais seria das mulheres.

“Esse discurso cresce como uma reação às conquistas feministas. À medida que as mulheres ampliam a autonomia, recusam relações abusivas e questionam os privilégios masculinos, alguns homens experimentam a igualdade como uma perda de direitos. O movimento 'red pill' transforma esse ressentimento em identidade coletiva”, declara Viviane.

No Brasil, a misoginia ainda não é tipificada como crime. Um projeto, já aprovado no Senado e enviado à Câmara dos Deputados para votação, propõe enquadrar a aversão e o discurso de ódio às mulheres como preconceito ou discriminação.

Ao analisar o caso do “ranking” sexual que expôs as universitárias, a advogada familiarista Renata De Vito, de Presidente Prudente (SP), discorre sobre as possibilidades de responsabilização dos suspeitos após as investigações policiais e considerando uma ausência de tipificação para a misoginia.

“Provando a culpa dos possíveis agressores, esse caso poderia entrar como importunação sexual, que é uma lei que já existe; talvez a Lei Carolina Dieckmann, considerando a exposição das fotos e o fato de que elas (as alunas) estão sendo faladas como se estivessem nuas nas imagens; uso indevido de imagem, pois eles captaram as fotos nas redes sociais sem autorização; e, obviamente, calúnia, difamação e injúria”, pontua.

A advogada também comenta sobre a atitude de algumas pessoas de tentarem minimizar o teor sexual da exposição à qual as alunas foram expostas. “É um ranking sexual, foram coletadas fotos nas redes sociais. Então, houve todo um trabalho, não foi uma brincadeirinha. Foi algo organizado e em termos que eu prefiro nem repetir”.

Renata fala, por fim, dos trabalhos de apuração da polícia após as denúncias das vítimas. “Se for provado e se os agressores forem identificados, vai ser analisado qual foi o ato de cada um, quem deu a ideia, quem fez o grupo, quem colheu as fotos e como isso foi organizado entre eles”, finaliza a advogada.

A advogada Renata De Vito esclarece que a misoginia ainda não é tipificada como crime no Brasil — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal/Divulgação

articles.title: Omar Aziz Eleições 2026: Candidato propõe zerar fila do Sisreg no AM | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato do PSD ao governo do Amazonas gravou programas para o horário eleitoral, nesta quarta-feira (26), onde comentou propostas para a saúde.
articles.summary: Omar Aziz, candidato ao governo do Amazonas nas Eleições 2026, detalha planos para a saúde, como a redução de filas e valorização de profissionais em Manaus.
articles.body:
Omar Aziz grava programa eleitoral em Manaus e apresenta propostas para saúde — Foto: Reprodução/Rede Amazônica

O candidato ao governo do Amazonas, Omar Aziz ( PSD ), cumpriu agenda de campanha na Zona Centro-Sul de Manaus na manhã desta quarta-feira (26). Ele gravou programas para o horário eleitoral. Durante a atividade, o candidato apresentou propostas para a área da saúde, como a redução de filas de exames e consultas, além da construção de hospitais e maternidades.

Omar Aziz disputa o cargo pela coligação "Força Amazonas", formada pelo Partido Social Democrático (PSD), Movimento Democrático Brasileiro ( MDB ) e Republicanos . O candidato já foi governador do estado entre 2010 e 2014.

Entre as prioridades para o setor de saúde, o candidato destacou a redução da fila de espera do Sistema Nacional de Regulação (Sisreg), a ampliação da rede hospitalar no interior e na capital, e o pagamento em dia dos profissionais da categoria.

"Primeiro nós vamos tratar da fila do Sisreg, imediatamente. Em 100 dias, com investimento, parcerias com clínicas e hospitais privados tentar ou diminuir, zerar a fila do Sisreg", afirmou.

Ao detalhar os planos para o interior do estado e para o atendimento maternal, Omar Aziz defendeu a descentralização dos serviços para evitar o deslocamento de pacientes para Manaus.

"Segundo nós precisamos construir sete a oito hospitais regionais de 150 leitos no interior para que essas pessoas não precisem se deslocar pra capital e aqui ir para uma fila e não ser atendido, que é o que está acontecendo hoje. Terceiro pagar os profissionais de saúde porque tem profissionais que estão a seis, sete meses sem receber então se você não recebe você não produz e quando produz não produz com qualidade você valorizando os profissionais na área de saúde nós terá uma saúde condizente com o povo amazonense que está precisando disso", declarou.

A agenda do candidato continua no fim da tarde com uma reunião interna com lideranças do interior do Amazonas, às 17h. Às 18h, ele participa de um evento popular na Zona Norte de Manaus.

A campanha eleitoral começou no dia 16 de agosto em todo o país. Os candidatos já podem fazer propaganda nas ruas e na internet. Na TV e no rádio, a propaganda começa na sexta-feira (28). O primeiro turno das eleições será no dia 4 de outubro.

articles.title: Candidatos doam para as próprias campanhas valor acima do permitido | G1
articles.standfirst: Políticos podem usar dinheiro do próprio bolso nas campanhas, mas devem respeitar teto. Estouro pode gerar multas de até 100% o valor que ultrapassou o limite.
articles.summary: Políticos podem usar dinheiro do próprio bolso, mas devem respeitar teto. Estouro pode gerar multas de até 100% o valor que ultrapassou o limite.
articles.body:
Dados do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) consultados pelo g1 nesta quarta-feira (26) mostram que, até o momento, 1.768 candidatos declararam doações para as próprias campanhas para as eleições deste ano. O número ainda pode aumentar até o fim da campanha, à medida que novas doações forem registradas

Desse total, dois candidatos ultrapassaram o limite legal de autofinanciamento : Joaquim Passarinho (PL-PA), candidato à reeleição para deputado federal, e José Eduardo Botelho (MDB-MT), que busca manter sua vaga de deputado estadual.

🔎 A lei permite que o candidato coloque dinheiro na própria campanha, mas ele deve respeitar o limite de até 10% do teto total de gastos para o cargo, conforme valores fixados pelo TSE. O excesso pode gerar multa de até 100% do valor excedente e causar a rejeição das contas, mas não provoca de forma automática nem a cassação da candidatura nem uma eventual inelegibilidade. Isso depende da abertura de processos.

Em um caso julgado após as eleições de 2022, um candidato a deputado estadual no Pará estourou o limite de autofinanciamento em 318%. Ele teve as contas recusadas e recebeu multa equivalente a todo o valor excedente ( leia mais abaixo ).

Nas eleições deste ano, Joaquim Passarinho declarou uma doação de R$ 500 mil à própria campanha . O teto total de gastos fixado pelo TSE para uma candidatura a deputado federal é de R$ 3.176.572,53, o que permite o uso de até R$ 317,6 mil de recursos próprios. O deputado federal doou, portanto, R$ 182,3 mil acima do máximo autorizado .

Procurado pelo g1 , Joaquim Passarinho disse que não sabia do limite que deveria respeitar e que vai devolver o valor excedente ( veja a íntegra da nota do candidato mais abaixo ). O diretório do PL no Pará não respondeu.

Joaquim Passarinho (PL-PA), candidato a deputado federal, declarou R$ 500 mil em recursos próprios à campanha — Foto: Equipe de arte/g1

Já Botelho desembolsou R$ 200 mil em recursos próprios . Para quem é candidato a deputado estadual, o teto total de gastos é de R$ 1.270.629,01, o que permite ao candidato financiar a própria campanha com até R$ 127 mil. Neste caso, a doação superou o limite em R$ 72,9 mil .

Procurados, Botelho e o MDB não se manifestaram.

José Eduardo Botelho (MDB-MT), candidato a deputado estadual, declarou R$ 200 mil em recursos próprios à campanha — Foto: Equipe de Arte/g1

O excesso de ambos os candidatos representa 57,40% do limite de autofinanciamento. Os candidatos são os maiores doadores de suas campanhas. Passarinho doou o equivalente a 89% de tudo que arrecadou e Botelho, 90%.

Passarinho é engenheiro, mas fez carreira na política, seguindo os passos do tio Jarbas Passarinho, que foi governador do Pará, três vezes senador e ministro no governo de Fernando Collor .

Nesta eleição, o candidato declarou R$ 3,1 milhões em bens. O valor é 71% maior que o declarado em 2022 , cerca de R$ 1,8 milhão. Naquele ano, ele doou R$ 127 mil e também foi o maior doador de sua campanha, mas não ultrapassou o limite de autofinaciamento.

Botelho também tem longa carreira na política. Ele foi presidente da Assembleia Legislativa do Mato Grosso por quatro mandados consecutivos, desde 2017.

Em 2021, o Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ) suspendeu sua terceira posse no cargo, por considerar a nova recondução inconstitucional. A decisão foi revista um ano depois, e ele retornou à presidência, onde permaneceu até 2025.

Nesta eleição, o candidato declarou R$ 5,3 milhões em bens, valor 16% maior do que o declarado em 2022, cerca de R$ 4,6 milhões.

Especialistas consultados pelo g1 explicam que o descumprimento da regra de autofinanciamento não significa necessariamente que houve abuso do poder econômico, pois isso depende de análise da Justiça Eleitoral.

Para Michel Bertoni Soares, advogado eleitoral e mestre em Direito Político e Econômico pela Universidade Presbiteriana Mackenzie, a análise não deve considerar apenas quanto o candidato ultrapassou o limite de autofinanciamento, mas também o peso do valor excedente sobre toda a arrecadação da campanha .

“Um parâmetro seria se a irregularidade correspondesse a mais de 20% do total arrecadado pela campanha”, afirmou.

Por esse cálculo, o excesso de R$ 182.342,75 atribuído a Passarinho corresponde a 32,62% dos R$ 559 mil arrecadados por sua campanha. No caso de Botelho, os R$ 72.937,10 representam 33,15% dos R$ 220 mil arrecadados.

Segundo a advogada eleitoralista e mestre em direito Emma Roberta Bueno, o abuso de poder econômico estaria configurado se o valor do autofinanciamento possibilitasse ao candidato ter uma campanha mais cara do que o permitido, o que causaria a desigualdade da disputa.

"As contas desses candidatos deverão ser desaprovadas, mas a lei não impõem como sanção, nesses casos, a cassação e nem uma inelegibilidade. A desaprovação das contas tem apenas um caráter financeiro que determina a devolução de valores pelo uso indevido ou de forma não transparente", disse a especialista.

Gabriela Rollemberg, advogada eleitoralista, membro da Academia Brasileira de Direito Eleitoral e Político (Abradep) e cientista política, afirmou que é necessário verificar se os valores classificados como recursos próprios incluem pagamentos de serviços advocatícios ou contábeis, que não entram no limite de gastos nem no teto de autofinanciamento.

"Juridicamente, não é possível cravar a existência de infração sem antes auditar a prestação de contas", explica a advogada.

A legislação prevê multa de até 100% da quantia que excedeu o limite. Isso significa que, no patamar máximo, Passarinho poderia receber multa de R$ 182.342,75 e Botelho, de R$ 72.937,10.

❗O percentual máximo, porém, não é aplicado automaticamente. A Justiça Eleitoral pode graduar a multa e decidir pela aprovação com ressalvas ou pela desaprovação das contas, considerando o valor absoluto, a proporção da irregularidade sobre a arrecadação total e a existência de outras falhas.

“A multa é de até 100%, mas o julgador pode se movimentar dentro desse limite de acordo com o caso concreto, exercendo um juízo de razoabilidade e proporcionalidade”, explicou Bertoni.

A multa também pode ser mantida mesmo que as contas sejam aprovadas com ressalvas, porque a sanção pelo excesso e o resultado geral da prestação de contas são análises distintas.

Segundo Rollemberg, a Justiça Eleitoral também considera a boa-fé do candidato, a transparência dos registros e uma eventual tentativa de corrigir a irregularidade.

A desaprovação das contas, sozinha, não provoca perda do mandato ou inelegibilidade. Nesses casos, o processo é encaminhado ao Ministério Público Eleitoral, que avalia se há elementos para uma investigação por abuso do poder econômico.

Somente em um processo próprio, com a comprovação da gravidade da conduta, podem ser aplicadas sanções como cassação do registro ou do diploma. A Lei Complementar nº 64 também prevê inelegibilidade por oito anos quando o abuso é reconhecido pela Justiça Eleitoral.

“O excesso de autofinanciamento por si só pode caracterizar abuso do poder econômico e levar à cassação, sem a necessidade de outros ilícitos cumulados. O elemento indispensável para essa sanção extrema é a comprovação da gravidade das circunstâncias ”, afirmou Rollemberg.

Candidato ultrapassou limite em 318% em 2022

Um levantamento do g1 nas prestações de contas das eleições de 2022 identificou 42 candidatos que ultrapassaram o limite de autofinanciamento, sendo 34 que disputavam vaga para deputado estadual, sete para deputado federal e um para o Senado.

O maior excesso identificado foi o de Jarbas Vasconcelos do Carmo (MDB), candidato a deputado estadual no Pará. Ele declarou R$ 532.140,28 em recursos próprios, embora o máximo permitido fosse R$ 127.062,90.

A diferença foi de R$ 405.077,38, o equivalente a 318,80% acima do teto . Jarbas não foi eleito e ficou como suplente.

Em abril de 2024, o Tribunal Regional Eleitoral do Pará desaprovou as contas e determinou a aplicação de multa equivalente a 100% do valor excedente.

A decisão também apontou ausência de extratos bancários completos, omissão de receitas e despesas, inconsistências na utilização do Fundo Especial de Financiamento de Campanha e recursos de origem não identificada. Por isso, não é possível atribuir a desaprovação das contas exclusivamente ao excesso de autofinanciamento.

Em uma ação separada referente às eleições de 2022, a Justiça Eleitoral afastou a caracterização de abuso de poder econômico no caso de Jarbas. A decisão não anulou nem substituiu o julgamento da prestação de contas: são processos com objetos diferentes.

Enquanto a prestação de contas verifica o cumprimento das regras financeiras e pode resultar em multa, o reconhecimento do abuso exige, em processo próprio, demonstração da gravidade da conduta e de sua capacidade de comprometer a normalidade ou a legitimidade da eleição.

Jarbas recorreu da desaprovação das contas. Os embargos de declaração foram rejeitados, e a Presidência do TRE-PA negou seguimento ao recurso especial apresentado contra o julgamento.

Wilson Paiva (PDT), candidato a deputado federal, doou para a própria campanha R$ 628 mil nas eleições de 2022 em São Paulo. O valor ultrapassou o teto em R$ 310.342,75, ou 97,7%. Ele também não foi eleito.

O TRE-SP desaprovou as contas e aplicou uma multa de R$ 155.171,37, correspondente a 50% do valor excedente.

O tribunal concluiu que, embora tenha ocorrido excesso ao limite estabelecido pela legislação, o valor não causou desequilíbrio do pleito, nem configurou abuso. “Não se impediu a correta identificação da origem dos recursos e o candidato possui lastro patrimonial para tanto”, diz a decisão.

Paiva tentou reverter a decisão, mas o recurso especial não foi admitido pela Presidência do TRE-SP. Ele, então, recorreu ao TSE, que manteve a decisão de origem em novembro de 2025.

O deputado Joaquim Passarinho não tinha, até então, ciência da incidência desse limite específico de 10% do teto de gastos para a utilização de recursos próprios na campanha.

Assim que tomou conhecimento da situação, decidiu adotar imediatamente as providências necessárias para a regularização, incluindo a devolução do valor que excedeu o limite permitido e o devido ajuste na prestação de contas.

Não houve qualquer intenção de descumprir a legislação eleitoral ou de obter vantagem com o aporte realizado. Os recursos são próprios, devidamente identificados e declarados à Justiça Eleitoral, e a situação será corrigida de forma transparente.

O deputado reafirma seu compromisso com a transparência e com o cumprimento da legislação eleitoral.

articles.title: Haddad critica pedágio free flow e pede revisão de contratos em SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato do PT ao governo de SP cumpre agenda de campanha nas cidades de Ourinhos e Assis nesta quarta-feira (26). Haddad também falou de revisão em contrato com a Sabesp.
articles.summary: Em campanha por Ourinhos e Assis, Haddad critica o pedágio free flow e defende a revisão de contratos da Sabesp para fortalecer a economia do interior de SP.
articles.body:
Fernando Haddad criticou sistema de pedágio free flow durante agenda de campanha em Ourinhos — Foto: Anderson Camargo/ TV TEM

Candidato ao governo de São Paulo pelo PT , Fernando Haddad criticou o sistema de pedágio free flow instalado em rodovias do estado e disse que os contratos devem ser revistos.

Haddad cumpre agenda de campanha nas cidades de Ourinhos e Assis nesta quarta-feira (26). Ele conversou com jornalistas em um restaurante da cidade depois que o encontro na Praça Mello Peixoto e a caminhada pelo centro da cidade terem sido cancelados por conta da chuva.

“O free flow está afetando a vida de muitos trabalhadores do interior. Gente está pagando para trabalhar. Então, está sendo mal planejada a instalação dos pórticos do free flow em todo o território do estado. Então, estão nos pedindo muita revisão do planejamento do Tarcísio, que está mal feito, segundo a maioria das pessoas ouvidas”, afirma.

🔎 O free flow é um sistema de pedágio eletrônico sem cancelas que permite cobrar a tarifa sem que o motorista precise parar ou reduzir a velocidade.

Na região centro-oeste paulista, o sistema foi implantado na pedágio no km 179 da Rodovia Laurentino Mascari (SP-333), entre Itápolis e Taquaritinga (SP) . O sistema também funciona em trechos da Rodovia Presidente Dutra (BR-116), da Rodovia Brigadeiro Faria Lima (SP-326) e Rodovia dos Tamoios (SPI-097/055).

Haddad defendeu também que outros contratos devem ser revisados e ressaltou a atuação das agências reguladoras no estado.

“Todo mundo é a favor de uma estrada segura, mas eu penso que nós precisamos rever algumas instalações que estão excessivas, com preço excessivo. Então, isso, tanto a Sabesp, contrato com a Sabesp ou contrato do Free Flow e, sobretudo na capital, os contratos da CPTM, dos trilhos, nós vamos passar para uma revisão muito criteriosa, fortalecendo as agências reguladoras do Estado que estão sucateadas.”

Questionado sobre a saída de grandes indústrias do interior de São Paulo, Haddad citou a guerra fiscal entre os estados e ressaltou a importância da reforma tributária no processo para reindustrializar o estado.

“A melhor coisa que aconteceu para o Estado de São Paulo nos últimos 40 anos foi a reforma tributária que o nosso Governo Federal fez e que entra em vigor a partir de 1º de janeiro. Para que fique claro a importância dessa reforma: qual foi a grande causa da desindustrialização de São Paulo? A guerra fiscal. Outros Estados dando benefícios fiscais para levar os empregos daqui. E levaram, uma boa parte. Com o fim da guerra fiscal, que é o objetivo número um da reforma tributária, nós vamos ter que nos preparar para reindustrializar o Estado de vários pontos de vista.”

Ainda em relação aos planos para o interior do estado, Haddad defendeu a retomada de propostas como o seguro rural.

“Tem algumas propostas muito importantes que nós queremos retomar. Primeiro, o seguro rural. O Plano Safra, ele é revolucionário. Ele é uma coisa que já impacta muito a agricultura em todo o país e, sobretudo, no estado de São Paulo. Então, nós temos que entender que o Plano Safra é o que está permitindo o Brasil bater recordes de produção e recordes de exportação”, completa.

O candidato cumpre agenda na região durante toda esta quarta-feira. De Ourinhos, ele segue para Assis onde participa de um ato político no Auditório da Associação Comercial.

articles.title: Enchentes no Nepal e China: Lula manifesta solidariedade | G1
articles.standfirst: Avalanche de lama na fronteira do Nepal com o Tibete deixou pelo menos 98 mortos e centenas de desaparecidos. Por ora, não há relatos de vítimas brasileiras, segundo o Itamaraty.
articles.summary: Após enchentes no Nepal e China deixarem 98 mortos, o presidente Lula prestou solidariedade e o Itamaraty informou que não há relatos de vítimas brasileiras na região.
articles.body:
O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ( PT ) manifestou nesta quarta-feira (26) solidariedade a familiares de vítimas e autoridades do Nepal e da China após inundações na fronteira dos dois países .

Nesta quarta, uma avalanche repentina na fronteira entre o Nepal e o Tibete, território controlado pelos chineses, deixou, até a última atualização, 98 mortos e mais de 800 desaparecidos .

Em uma rede social, Lula disse ter recebido as notícias sobre as enchentes "com muita tristeza".

"As imagens causam espanto e nos comovem a todos. Em nome dos brasileiros, expresso minha solidariedade aos governos dos dois países e a todos os afetados por esse desastre, especialmente às famílias das vítimas", disse o petista.

O Ministério das Relações Exteriores informou que, até o momento, não há relatos de vítimas brasileiras. O Itamaraty está acompanhando a situação.

Vídeos da região mostram cenas assustadoras: uma onda de lama desce o vale arrastando pontes, cobrindo um prédio do porto de Gyirong e engolindo vilas na área turística da região.

Até por volta das 12h, havia 98 mortes confirmadas e 844 desaparecidos (95 mortes e 579 desaparecidos no Nepal e 3 mortes e 265 desaparecidos no Tibete).

➡️ COMO É A REGIÃO? A área afetada é uma região de fronteira com apelo turístico e cercada por uma das cadeias de montanhas mais famosas do mundo (leia mais abaixo).

Embora não seja muito populosa, a região conecta diversas cidades e vilas e abriga usinas hidrelétricas e um porto, além de um posto fronteiriço entre o Nepal e a China. O posto é uma das principais portas de entrada e saída para quem viaja entre os dois países.

O Conselho de Turismo do Nepal informou que 384 viajantes que estão no país, sendo 341 estrangeiros, estão desaparecidos após a inundação.

A avalanche atingiu Syabrubesi, ponto de partida da famosa trilha do Langtang, e outras áreas frequentadas por viajantes que fazem o passeio de peregrinação hindu ao Kailash Mansarovar.

Equipes de resgate carregam uma pessoa atingida por uma enchente repentina em Devghat, no distrito de Nuwakot, no Nepal. — Foto: PRAKASH MATHEMA/AFP

articles.title: Pentagon claims to have found ‘hidden’ files on final days of the Afghanistan war
articles.summary: Republicans have long accused former President Joe Biden's administration of covering up mistakes made in the final days of the conflict.
articles.body:
Pentagon officials on Wednesday claimed they have uncovered classified documents that were "hidden away in safes where they would not be found" that shed new light on the chaotic end to the U.S. war in Afghanistan five years ago — but declined to offer public details of the revelations.

The claim comes hours before Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is scheduled to participate in a Pentagon ceremony to upgrade the valor awards for service members who served at the Kabul International Airport during the final days of the conflict.

The end of the war — and the final days of the U.S. occupation, when 13 American service members were killed guarding the airport — have been a focal point of Republican criticism of former President Joe Biden's foreign policy decisions while in office.

GOP lawmakers have accused Biden of too abruptly ending military operations in Afghanistan, endangering American troops and handing over control of the country to the Taliban. Democratic supporters argue Biden's move brought to an end two decades of open-ended military missions that did little to improve national security.

The White House has labeled the final days of the war "one of the most shameful and heartbreaking moments in our nation's collective memory." Pentagon leaders established a new Afghanistan Withdrawal Special Review Panel to examine the decisions leading up to the American exit from Kabul and determine who deserves blame for the U.S. deaths there.

Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell, chair of the panel, in April announced plans to upgrade valor awards given to troops serving at the airport in August 2021 to "more accurately reflect the extreme risk" the troops faced, claiming that the Biden administration had "inappropriately downgraded" earlier honors.

Parnell on Wednesday released a video message on social media claiming the ongoing review has uncovered more improprieties by the previous administration, although he did not provide any details.

"The deeper we look, the more there is to look at," he said in the message. "We are finding things that we did not expect.".

He added that his team had "recovered highly relevant classified documents, material that should have been disclosed, stashed, and hidden away in safes where they would not be found. And after the team reviewed these documents, it became clear why someone tried to hide them."

Parnell said that troops who served in Afghanistan "are owed the full picture of how and why those decisions were made, and we're going to give it to them." He did not provide any specifics on a timeline for clearer details on the new findings.

Democratic lawmakers have questioned the intentions of the reviews and criticized the slant of Republican-led hearings on Capitol Hill blaming the 20-year war largely on Democratic presidents.

House Republicans in recent years have accused Biden administration officials of ignoring intelligence reports in the days before the fatal terrorist bombing at the airport, a charge that military officials have rebuffed.

images.caption: Pentagon claims to have found ‘hidden’ files on final days of the Afghanistan war

articles.title: Why high defense spending is bad for America
articles.summary: Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth recently testified before the Senate that, should Congress fail to pass the entire requested $1.5 trillion defense budget, it would put the United States in danger. Contrary to Hegseth’s testimony, however, this threat inflation and oversized defense budget only makes America weaker.
articles.body:
Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth recently testified before the Senate that, should Congress fail to pass the entire requested $1.5 trillion defense budget, it would put the U.S. in danger .

Hegseth justified higher defense spending by inflating the threats America faces and presenting worst-case scenarios. That same week, the House passed the fiscal 2027 National Defense Authorization Act as well as the Trump administration’s latest reconciliation bill.

Contrary to Hegseth’s testimony, however, this threat-inflation and oversized defense budget only makes America weaker.

For starters, it fails to align spending to America’s strategic goals. Lawmakers claim that with all the threats the U.S. is up against, it cannot risk cutting any weapons or defense programs. This budget does not even cut systems like the B-1B bomber, an aircraft with no stealth capabilities and a higher operational cost than the B-52, or the Minuteman III, a nuclear missile that is decades old and increases crisis instability between nations on account of its first-strike vulnerability. This keeps the U.S. wasting money on weapons that don not strengthen the nation’s security.

On top of that, policymakers want to add even more unneeded weapons to America’s arsenal. The Pentagon seeks to build battleships , a naval vessel disused since World War II, and is pushing for development of a national missile defense that many nuclear experts deem both wasteful and dangerous , as it would incentivize America’s adversaries to launch a surprise attack in order to have a better chance at their missiles getting through. Some of these billions put toward unneeded weapons could instead be used for useful military investments, like munitions production .

The Trump administration waves off the long-term costs — namely, the interest that comes from federal borrowing. This makes it seem like an increased defense budget doesn’t affect the average American, allowing policymakers to avoid increasing taxes or making immediate cuts to social services. But this just punts the costs to future generations. The U.S. already borrowed money to pay for America’s Global War on Terror and the Iraq War ; keeping the tab running will only add to this deferred cost, eventually forcing citizens to choose between massive cuts to social programs and tax hikes or cutting defense programs to help pay it off.

President Trump’s colossal defense budget will only degrade the nation’s economic strength and wellbeing. Defense spending is the most economically wasteful of all federal spending. Advocates for higher defense spending argue that the U.S. sets aside only a small percentage of its GDP to pay for defense, making more spending possible. But this framing leaves out the fact that these billions of dollars were not needed in the first place and could have been saved for higher priorities.

So no, Hegseth and Trump’s high defense budget will not strengthen the U.S. Quite the opposite— it will weaken Americans’ economic security, weaken America’s economic power, and weaken the country’s national security. Instead, the Trump administration and Congress should cut the defense budget, and with it, America’s wars and overseas commitments.

This would avoid costly conflicts and commitments, keep the U.S. secure and strengthen its economic power. And economic strength is important for a country’s security . In the event of a conflict, money is needed to build weapons, and decent roads and railways are required to transport military equipment and supplies across the country. Rather than waste money on unnecessary programs, the U.S. government must get America’s house in order and serve the people.

Benjamin D. Giltner is a defense and foreign policy analyst at the Cato Institute .

images.caption: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth testifies at a Senate Appropriations subcommittee on defense hearing on the budget request for the Department of Defense, Tuesday, May 12, 2026, in Washington. (AP Photo/Alex Brandon)

articles.title: From a theme park to moss: The things named after Dolly Parton
articles.summary: You may have to do some trekking to find some things named after Dolly Parton.
articles.body:
(NEXSTAR) – Dolly Parton, the beloved country music icon and philanthropist with humble beginnings in East Tennessee, died Tuesday at the age of 80 . Her name will undoubtedly live on, fueled by her extensive music catalogue , her foundation that sends free books to children , her charitable work , and a few other things you may not know bear her name.

For those who live in or around Tennessee, several sites may immediately come to mind.

There is, of course, Dollywood , the theme park Parton co-owned in Pigeon Forge, Tennessee. The park originally opened in 1961 as Rebel Railroad, and in 1977, it became Silver Dollar City Tennessee. Then, in 1986, Parton became a co-owner, and the park was renamed Dollywood.

The site attracts millions of visitors annually and generates more than 19,000 regional jobs, according to The Greater Pigeon Forge Chamber of Commerce .

Travelers may also be familiar with a new venture sporting Parton’s name: Dolly’s Tennessean Travel Stop . Themed around the Tennessee native, the travel stop is located in Cornersville, Tennessee, just off Interstate 65, and opened in June, Nexstar’s WATE reported . Additional travel stops could open in the future.

That travel stop also sells Parton’s coffee brand, “Cup of Ambition,” which she unveiled earlier this year. WATE reported in June that the coffee, inspired by her hit song “9 to 5,” was expected to be available nationwide soon.

Should you ever travel to Parton’s hometown of Sevierville, Tennessee, you may drive on part of Dolly Parton Parkway along US 411. Sevierville has several Parton landmarks to visit, including a statue on the county courthouse’s lawn and multiple murals inspired by the local legend.

Scheduled to open later this year in Nashville is Dolly Parton’s Songteller Hotel , which, on the third floor, will also house Dolly’s Life of Many Colors Museum . The site’s general manager told Nexstar’s WKRN last year that the “project is truly Dolly’s love letter to her fans and a love letter to Nashville in particular.” The museum is expected to open in October while the hotel is set to start taking reservations in September.

There’s also Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library . When it opened in 1995, the goal was to send free books to children in Sevier County, where Parton grew up. It grew immensely, now serving 1 in 6 children in the U.S. who are under the age of 5. A spokesperson for the Dollywood Company confirmed to Nexstar on Tuesday that the free books will still be sent to eligible children.

While a theme park and a travel stop and a statue are easy to spot, there are a few other natural features named after Parton.

In 2015, scientists named a species of lichen discovered in the Appalachian region after Parton. Japewiella dollypartoniana is found from Maine to Georgia, commonly on branches of trees and shrubs at middle to high elevations. The researchers said the name honors Parton and her rise “from humble roots to stardom.”

A study published in 2019 named a 460 million-year-old moss species found in Tennessee after Dolly Parton. Dollyphyton boucotii was found in rock deposits near Dollywood, hence the name.

There is also, of course, Dolly the sheep , the first cloned mammal created from an adult cell. More specifically, Dolly the sheep was grown from a single cell collected from the mammary glands, located in a female’s chest. Parton later told The Guardian that she was “flattered” that the sheep, who died in 2003, was named after her.

“I was sorry when she died,” Parton told the outlet, “though I don’t want to be cloned myself.”

Nexstar’s Alix Martichoux contributed to this report.

images.caption: Dolly Parton poses for a picture before the Carnegie Medal of Philanthropy Ceremony at Gotham Hall in New York on Oct. 13, 2022. Parton released a new album “Rockstar.” (AP Photo/Andres Kudacki, File)

articles.title: Tim Curry, star of ‘Rocky Horror’ and ‘It,’ dead at 80
articles.summary: Tim Curry, the British actor whose long career included a cult role in “The Rocky Horror Picture Show,” has died. He was 80 years old.
articles.body:
(NEXSTAR) – Tim Curry, the British actor whose long career included a cult role in “The Rocky Horror Picture Show,” has died. He was 80 years old.

He died at his home in Los Angeles, his manager Marcia Hurwitz confirmed to The Associated Press on Wednesday. The cause of death was not immediately released.

The Los Angeles Police Department told Nexstar’s KTLA that officers responded to a home in North Hollywood on Tuesday night for the death of a man in his 80s but gave no further details.

The actor had suffered health issues since a stroke in 2012. He attended a 50th anniversary screening of “The Rocky Horror Picture Show” in a wheelchair last year.

“I still can’t walk, which is why I’m in this silly chair, and that’s very limiting. So I won’t be singing and I won’t be dancing very soon. I still have real problems with my left leg,” he told The Hollywood Reporter at the time.

Playing Dr. Frank-N-Furter in “Rocky Horror” may have been Curry’s big break, but it was far from his only big acting credit. He was also known for playing the scary clown Pennywise in “It,” Rooster in the 1982 adaptation of “Annie,” Wadsworth in 1985’s “Clue” and Roger Corwin in “Charlie’s Angels” in 2000.

“Hollywood tends to use European actors, especially English ones, as villains because they prefer heroes to be Americans. I think we come with a certain amount of style, which is hard for American actors to acquire,” Curry told the Associated Press in 1997.

His IMDb page lists more than 240 other acting and voice acting credits dating back to 1968.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

images.caption: LOS ANGELES, CA – OCTOBER 30: Actor Tim Curry attends the 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment Celebrates 40th Anniversary Of “The Rocky Horror Picture Show” at Los Angeles City Hall on October 30, 2015 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Earl Gibson III/WireImage)

articles.body:
What’s happening with mail-in voting? An emergency Supreme Court ruling centered on President Trump’s executive order around the practice has led to a flood of questions , just days before states start sending out ballots.

Join Legal Affairs Editor Zach Schonfeld and Legal Affairs Reporter Sophie Brams as they break down the ruling , the courts’ options for the midterms and what it means for your ballot.

Plus, they’ll analyze the breaking news of the $17 billion settlement between states and Meta in the middle of their landmark child safety trial and preview tomorrow’s hearing on the future of the Kennedy Center renovations.

articles.title: Iowa’s Democratic governor candidate: Kamala Harris shouldn’t run in 2028
articles.summary: Rob Sand, the Democratic gubernatorial nominee in Iowa, said in an interview released Wednesday that former Vice President Kamala Harris should not run for president in 2028. “Nope,” Sand remarked, after Politico’s Jonathan Martin asked him whether Harris should seek the Democratic nomination again. He also brushed off questions about Harris, who ran two unsuccessful…
articles.body:
Rob Sand, the Democratic gubernatorial nominee in Iowa, said in an interview released Wednesday that former Vice President Kamala Harris should not run for president in 2028 .

“Nope,” Sand remarked , after Politico’s Jonathan Martin asked him whether Harris should seek the Democratic nomination again.

He also brushed off questions about Harris, who ran two unsuccessful bids for the White House, potentially campaigning for him.

“No thanks,” the Iowa state auditor said, when pressed on the issue.

“Let’s move on,” he added. “We need some new leadership.”

Harris has not definitively said whether she will run for president again in 2028, but she said in April she “might” do so.

“I’m thinking about it,” the former vice president told the Rev. Al Sharpton at the National Action Network’s annual convention .

Sand is facing off against Republican businessman Zach Lahn in the race to succeed outgoing Iowa Gov. Kim Reynolds (R). A Democrat has not won an Iowa gubernatorial election since former Gov. Chet Culver (D) two decades ago.

A recent poll by Suffolk University found Sand leading Lahn, with 48 percent support to the Republican’s 44 percent. Sand’s lead was within the margin of error of 4.4 percentage points.

The only Democrat elected to statewide office in 2022, Sand has served as state auditor since 2019. The Democratic gubernatorial nominee has criticized his own party, saying blue states California and New York “are not utopia” earlier this month.

“You can put something in a place, and it does okay for a little while. But if it’s there for too long, it gets unbalanced,” Sand said at the Des Moines Register Political Soapbox. “You gotta take it out and put something else in.

“I just described crop rotation, and that works for politicians the same way it does for corn and beans, ladies and gentlemen. Time to rotate the crops in the capitol building,” he added, referring to the GOP’s grip on the Hawkeye State.

During his interview with Martin, Sand also turned down the hypothetical of former President Biden campaigning for him.

“No. Can he even do that right now? I’m sorry,” Sand said of the 83-year-old Biden , who has prostate cancer .

images.caption: Iowa Democratic gubernatorial canddiate Rob Sand and former Vice President Kamala Harris. (AP Photo/Charlie Neibergall/Meg Kinnard)

articles.title: Green New Dodge: El-Sayed runs from policy as newly surfaced deleted posts show years of support
articles.summary: Abdul El-Sayed refused to defend the Green New Deal on air, but deleted posts show he once wrote "I believe in a Green New Deal" in all caps.
articles.body: Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed told Fox News host Jesse Watters on Monday that he would not defend the Green New Deal when confronted with his past support for the progressive climate proposal, a notable shift from years of publicly embracing it by name. "Look, I’m not going to defend the Green New Deal," El-Sayed told Watters after the host confronted him over his past support for the proposal. When Watters reiterated that El-Sayed was on record supporting it, El-Sayed redirected the discussion toward lowering energy costs and creating Michigan jobs by prioritizing renewables. Michigan, which Trump won in 2024 but lost in 2020, is shaping up to have one of the most competitive Senate races in the country, with the likely narrow results in the state potentially determining control of Congress. Critics charge that El-Sayed is downplaying some of his past beliefs and scrubbing his online footprint to appear more moderate, and therefore more palatable, to Michigan voters. UNEARTHED CLIP EXPOSES MORE ANTI-POLICE RHETORIC AS EL-SAYED GETS GRILLED FOR DELETING SOCIAL MEDIA POSTS Though El-Sayed declined to defend the Green New Deal in front of a national audience, he previously hasn’t been so shy. A Fox News Digital review of El-Sayed's deleted social media posts, preserved via the Internet Archive, uncovered dozens of examples of the Michigan Senate hopeful defending the Green New Deal by name. "Rather than announcing the next iteration of this or that car at [the North American International Auto Show 2019], I’d love to see automakers announce that they support the #GreenNewDeal," El-Sayed wrote in January of that year. On the primary campaign trail, Rep. Haley Stevens criticized El-Sayed over his past support for the Green New Deal on the grounds that it could lead to job losses in the automobile manufacturing industry. FOX NEWS POWER RANKINGS: AS DEMOCRATS TURN LEFT, BLACK VOTERS TAP THE BRAKES "The struggle for the Green New Deal uplifts the struggle for racial justice," El-Sayed wrote in April 2019. The Green New Deal is a 2019 progressive policy framework floated by Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., and Sen. Ed Markey, D-Mass., that seeks to gradually transition the United States’ electrical grid away from fossil fuels. Their plan has become synonymous with the left-wing faction of the Democratic Party, leading many Democrats running in competitive races to distance themselves from it. In another post, from September 2019, El-Sayed wrote, "I believe in a Green New Deal" five times in all caps. He also suggested that the Green New Deal is essential to preserve freedom of speech because there can be no First Amendment "without the freedom to breathe the breath you have to take to speak in the first place." "The #GreenNewDeal doesn’t center polar bears or glaciers, it centers those children forced to breath (sic.) in corporate pollution in their communities," El-Sayed wrote. "I stand with the Green New Deal because it stands for those kids." WATCH: SURFACED VIDEOS OF DEM SENATE CANDIDATE BACKING 'DEFUND THE POLICE' CONTRADICT RECENT DENIALS CNN previously reported that El-Sayed scrubbed large swathes of his commentary from the internet prior to announcing his run for Senate. The deletions appear to have been selective, as he still has some posts up from before he launched his campaign. In his since-deleted social media posts, El-Sayed endorsed the "defund the police" movement, argued cities spent too much policing poverty and described police departments as "standing armies we deploy against our own people." In a separate YouTube video that was later hidden, he floated replacing the Second Amendment’s right to bear arms with a constitutional right to healthcare and called Border Patrol agents "white supremacists" while blaming American policies for migration from struggling nations. Though El-Sayed regularly mentioned the Green New Deal on X prior to running for Senate, he has not posted the phrase even once since announcing his candidacy, a review found. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The El-Sayed campaign did not respond to a request for comment when reached by Fox News Digital on Tuesday.

articles.title: How I convinced Chris Wallace to interview Dolly Parton
articles.summary: “Should I interview Dolly Parton?” I looked up from my desk to find Chris Wallace standing in my office. This was not a particularly unusual occurrence, since Wallace’s office was next to mine, and we would sometimes pop in on each other to compare notes. I was the managing editor of Fox News’s D.C. bureau…
articles.body:
I looked up from my desk to find Chris Wallace standing in my office.

This was not a particularly unusual occurrence, since Wallace’s office was next to mine, and we would sometimes pop in on each other to compare notes. I was the managing editor of Fox News’s D.C. bureau at the time, while Wallace hosted “Fox News Sunday.”

“Yes,” I replied without knowing further context. “You should absolutely interview her. She is nothing less than a national treasure.”

Wallace expressed surprise at my enthusiasm, saying I didn’t strike him as a country music aficionado.

“I’m not,” I replied. “It’s not about the genre. It’s about her songwriting.”

Wallace was known for hard-hitting interviews on policy and politics, so I worried that he might consider Dolly Parton a bit out of his lane. I decided to put on the full-court press.

“You have to interview her,” I blurted. “I honestly believe she’s one of the greatest songwriters America has ever produced.”

I stipulated that I was not an expert on songwriting or country music or even Dolly Parton. But of the dozen or so country songs I’ve ever downloaded (amid thousands of songs in other genres), all of them are by Dolly Parton.

“Not just made famous by Parton,” I emphasized to Wallace. “Actually written by her. I mean, you just cannot ignore the enormity of her songwriting.”

For starters, it is well known that Parton wrote two of her most monumental songs — “Jolene” and “I Will Always Love You” — in one epic creative burst. (It was long believed she wrote them on the same day, but Parton later clarified the process may have stretched into several days.)

The results of that one burst would have been enough to assure the legacy of any mortal songwriter. But Parton wrote so many more masterpieces during an astonishing career that spanned seven decades.

Poignant songs of sadness, like “Coat of Many Colors” and “To Daddy.” Dark songs of betrayal, like “Little Sparrow” and “Dagger Through the Heart.” Wistful songs of lost love, like “The Grass is Blue” and “Do I Ever Cross Your Mind?”

So much melancholy for an otherwise upbeat icon who seemed to radiate good vibes at all times. Fittingly, amid all those sorrowful songs, there was a thread of hopefulness that became her trademark. Take, for example, the opening lines to yet another Parton classic, “Light of a Clear Blue Morning”:

But everything’s gonna work out just fine

Of course, Wallace didn’t need much convincing. He jumped at the chance to interview Dolly Parton. And given my admiration for her, he invited me to the interview.

As the big day approached, I mentally prepared to thank Parton for the various specific songs that meant so much to me. But when she walked through that door in February 2018, I chickened out and resorted to a vague statement about how I was a big fan.

Parton proved just as sweet and down-to-earth as you’d expect. She chatted good-naturedly and posed for a photo. She had me sit down while she remained standing because I’m so tall (6 feet, 7 inches) and she was so short (5 feet). Honestly, she couldn’t have been nicer.

The interview took place at the Library of Congress because Parton was about to present the library with her newest children’s book, “Coat of Many Colors.”

Based on the song of the same name, the book tells the story of Parton’s mother sewing rags into a coat for Dolly, one of 12 children in a family that eked out a hardscrabble existence in the Great Smoky Mountains of east Tennessee.

Of course, Parton would go on to enormous success. Her signature charity, Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library, has given hundreds of millions of books to schoolchildren. Parton herself literally went from rags to riches.

At the end of her interview with Wallace, Parton burst into song, a cappella, reminding us, yet again, of why she will be remembered as one of America’s greatest songwriters:

And my coat of many colors that my mama made for me

Made only from rags, but I wore it so proudly

And although we had no money, I was rich as I could be

In my coat of many colors my mama made for me

images.caption: Bill Sammon and Dolly Parton pose for a photo.

articles.title: Blue states launch new suit to stop Trump’s mail-in voting restrictions
articles.summary: Democratic-controlled states brought a new lawsuit challenging the Trump administration’s mail-in voting restrictions on Wednesday, hoping they’ll find better success after the Supreme Court ruled they sued prematurely. The high court found the states had no right to sue over the president’s executive order that he signed in the spring. But it left open the possibility that someone…
articles.body:
Democratic-controlled states brought a new lawsuit challenging the Trump administration’s mail-in voting restrictions on Wednesday, hoping they’ll find better success after the Supreme Court ruled they sued prematurely.

The high court found the states had no right to sue over the president’s executive order that he signed in the spring. But it left open the possibility that someone could still try to sue over the U.S. Postal Service’s plan to implement it.

The Postal Service formally published its final rule on Wednesday. The states argue it means their case is now ripe.

“Congress has not afforded USPS any authority whatsoever to set rules for federal elections or mail voting, even though Americans have cast ballots by mail for generations,” the lawsuit states, using an abbreviation for the U.S. Postal Service.

The case is co-led by California, Massachusetts, Nevada and Washington. It heads to U.S. District Judge Indira Talwani, an appointee of former President Obama who has been overseeing the legal fight for months.

The Hill has reached out to a Department of Justice (DOJ) spokesperson for comment.

The Postal Service’s final rule mandates that states’ mail-in ballots meet design requirements — such as unique barcodes and an official logo — and that the states upload lists of voters who are eligible to vote by mail. If a ballot doesn’t meet the specifications or someone isn’t on the submitted list, the Postal Service will refuse to deliver it. It’s part of President Trump’s broader, years-long campaign targeting mail voting.

The president’s critics have condemned his order as overreaching into states’ authority to manage their own elections.

The states’ new lawsuit landed just as the judge cleared the way for USPS. Talwani on Wednesday agreed the Supreme Court’s recent directive compels her to wipe all her previous injunctions.

Even so, she cautioned that the plaintiffs could now have a case that USPS has finalized its rule.

The clock is ticking, with some states set to start sending out mail ballots in a matter of days.

articles.title: Appeals court declines to toss McIver case as panel splits on selective prosecution claims
articles.summary: A federal appeals court declined to toss the case against Rep. LaMonica McIver (D-N.J.), even as the panel split over a matter in which she is accused of attacking law enforcement with her forearms in a scuffle with immigration officials. The ruling on Wednesday from the 3rd Circuit Court of Appeals comes as McIver has pushed to…
articles.body:
A federal appeals court declined to toss the case against Rep. LaMonica McIver (D-N.J.), even as the panel split over a matter in which she is accused of attacking law enforcement with her forearms in a scuffle with immigration officials.

The ruling on Wednesday from the 3rd Circuit Court of Appeals comes as McIver has pushed to get the case dismissed on various grounds, including that her visit to the Delaney Hall detention facility was carried out in her role as a legislative official and should be protected by prosecution under the Speech or Debate Clause.

The three-judge panel declined to toss the case on a number of grounds raised by McIver, finding that while her inspection of Delaney Hall was protected under the clause, her intervention in the arrest of Newark Mayor Ras Baraka (D) was not.

But one judge dissented, saying McIver’s “plausibly incidental contact” with one of the officers came as she was being impeded from carrying out her legislative duties by touring the controversial detention center.

He also touched on McIver’s claims that the case amounted to a selective prosecution , saying the lawmaker “presented enough [evidence] to obtain discovery on whether this prosecution ‘was intended to prevent [her] exercise of a fundamental right’” to conduct legislative oversight.

The pending arrest against Baraka — who no longer faces charges in the matter — ignited chaos between Democrats there to tour the facility and immigration officials on site.

McIver is accused of having “slammed her forearm into the body” of one immigration officer and “using each of her forearms to forcibly strike” a second.

The appeals court determined those actions were not protected by the clause.

“The Speech or Debate Clause does not provide a blanket protection over ‘all things in any way related to the legislative process,’” Judge Cindy Chung wrote in the majority opinion.

“The nature of the conduct charged in Count One is non legislative. Congresswoman McIver’s physical contact with Victim-1 was not ‘integral’ to the ‘deliberative and communicative processes by which Members participate in committee and House proceedings.’”

The ruling determined charges related to those two incidents should stand but remanded the case back to the district court to review a third count that broadly incorporated all “efforts to hinder, impede the arrest of the Mayor.”

A second opinion from Judge Thomas Ambro dissented in part, saying his colleagues were too quick to determine that some of her actions could not be considered tied to her legislative role, saying the second count faced by McIver was at least “ambiguously” legislative.

“When an Executive Branch official prevents a Member from entering a DHS [Department of Homeland Security] facility, she is denied effective access to an oversight inspection, the investigative tool federal law supplies Members in this context,” Ambro wrote, adding that “her access to the facility depended on circumventing him somehow.”

Ambro also said the court should at least grant McIver further discovery on whether she is being selectively prosecuted.

He wrote that among lawmakers’ protections are “freedom from fear that the Executive will use criminal prosecution to punish legislators for their oversight and political opposition.”

“My colleagues believe vindication of this right is beyond our jurisdiction. I disagree. And where, as here, a legislator has presented evidence that her prosecution was brought as an act of political retaliation, I would allow her discovery into the truth of the matter—not only for her own sake but to safeguard the independence of our legislative bodies,” Ambro wrote, saying she deserved to know “whether [the case] punishes her for doing her job as a Member of Congress with specific oversight responsibilities.”

articles.title: Maverick Democrat surges with Republicans as his own party turns on him, stoking talk of GOP switch
articles.summary: John Fetterman now holds a 73% favorability among Pennsylvania Republicans, surpassing Dave McCormick's 63%, as party switch speculation grows.
articles.body: Sen. John Fetterman of Pennsylvania, a centrist Democrat known for bashing his party's left flank, is more popular among Keystone State Republicans than their own GOP senator, Sen. Dave McCormick, according to a new poll. The release of the poll this week by the New York Times, Philadelphia Inquirer and Siena University is further evidence that Fetterman, who at times breaks with his party and aligns with President Donald Trump, and who is a frequent guest on the Fox News Channel, has become increasingly popular among Republicans. The survey may boost speculation that the first-term senator could potentially bolt the Democrats and become a Republican. But Fetterman has denied that he plans to leave the Democratic Party. Nearly 3 in 4 Republican registered voters in Pennsylvania (73%) held a favorable opinion of Fetterman, according to the poll. That's 10 points higher than the 63% of Republicans in the state who viewed McCormick favorably. DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB The 73% of Republicans who view Fetterman favorably is a major increase from the 25% who said the same thing in 2024, two years after the senator was elected. But Fetterman's standing among Democrats continued to sink, according to the poll. Just 22% of registered Democrats in Pennsylvania said they had a favorable view of Fetterman, while 63% viewed him unfavorably. That's a dramatic reversal from two years ago, when 74% of Democrats viewed Fetterman favorably. The survey also indicated that by a 49%-35% margin independents held a favorable view of Fetterman. Matt Beynon, a veteran Pennsylvania-based Republican consultant, told Fox News Digital, "I think a lot of Republicans appreciate the fact that Senator Fetterman is willing to stick his thumb in the radical wing of his party’s eye on issues like antisemitism." WHAT THE LATEST FOX NEWS POWER RANKINGS IN THE MIDTERM RACES SHOW Fetterman's growing popularity among Republicans has fueled speculation that he leave the Democratic Party before potentially facing a primary challenge when he's up for re-election in 2028. The senator, who is a strong supporter of Israel, has increasingly railed against fellow Democrats who have criticized Israeli leaders over their ongoing war against Hamas in Gaza. Fetterman has said he has "no plans" to leave the Democratic Party. But he added if Democrats officially became the "anti-Israel party," count him out. "My long-term concern has been with the Democratic Party, as I am a member of that, is that our party is going to back away and turn their back to Israel," he said last month at a Hill Nation Summit in Washington, D.C. "If our party ever becomes, and just makes it official, the anti-Israel party, that’s when I would leave because that’s been a moral clarity for me." SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) and other Senate Republicans have reached out to Fetterman regarding a party switch. "I have had conversations with him in the past, as have many of my colleagues about the challenges he faces in his caucus. And there are many of us who, I think, would welcome the opportunity to have him join the Republican conference, but ultimately that’s a decision that’s up to him," Thune told reporters in July. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP But Beynon said that regardless of Fetterman's growing popularity among Republicans, "when it comes time for the Senator’s re-election campaign in 2028, those same voters will be reminded that John Fetterman votes with Democrats more than 90% of the time." Fox News Digital reached out to the senator's office for comment regarding the new poll, but did not receive a response at the time this story was published.

articles.title: Charlamagne knocks Jeffries over Kushner meeting: ‘Yo Hakeem, we don’t believe you’
articles.summary: Charlamagne Tha God slammed House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.) over his private meeting with Jared Kushner, President Trump’s son-in-law, accusing the Democratic leader of undermining his own attacks on Trump and his allies. “Yo Hakeem, we don’t believe you,” Charlamagne said Tuesday on “The Breakfast Club,” days after The New York Times reported Sunday…
articles.body:
Charlamagne Tha God slammed House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.) over his private meeting with Jared Kushner, President Trump’s son-in-law, accusing the Democratic leader of undermining his own attacks on Trump and his allies.

“Yo Hakeem, we don’t believe you,” Charlamagne said Tuesday on “The Breakfast Club,” days after The New York Times reported Sunday that Jeffries and Kushner met privately ahead of November’s midterms.

Jeffries had sought to quell backlash over the meeting by saying “no one from the Trump Cartel is getting a pass.” The House Democratic leader has said Kushner, an informal Trump administration adviser, initiated the meeting. The two reportedly met to discuss common ground issues such as housing and affordability.

Charlamagne argued Democrats shouldn’t use dire language to describe Trump and his movement while privately seeking common ground with people in the president’s orbit.

“Saying people are threats to democracy and fascists and crooks — when you say that, and then we have private meetings with them, working with them, it undermines all of that,” he said.

Kushner, who is married to Trump’s eldest daughter, Ivanka Trump, does not hold an official position in the administration, but he has worked as a foreign envoy in major conflicts, including in Iran.

News of the meeting sparked criticism from some Democrats, prompting Jeffries to defend his decision. In a video posted Monday, Jeffries said he was willing to discuss ways to bring down costs for Americans but insisted that would not stop Democrats from scrutinizing the Trump administration.

“We’re going to follow the facts, apply the law and be guided by the Constitution beginning on day one. And hold the crooks accountable.”

“That’s why Hakeem is getting this smoke, that’s why he’s getting this backlash from people,” he said.

He also questioned why Democratic leaders appear more willing to find common ground with Trump allies than with colleagues in their own party, including progressives.

“I also don’t understand why Democrats have more smoke with people in their own party, like the DSA [Democratic Socialists of America] or anyone labeled a socialist, than they do with MAGA,” Charlamagne said.

images.caption: Charlamagne Tha God poses for a photo at Pullman Yards on April 27, 2024, in Atlanta.

articles.title: Philadelphia DA says he'll keep piece of Trump's White House ballroom 'after we all blow it up'
articles.summary: Philadelphia District Attorney Larry Krasner said Tuesday he expects President Donald Trump’s White House ballroom to one day be blown up in an “official ceremony."
articles.body: Philadelphia District Attorney Larry Krasner said Tuesday he was going to keep a piece of President Donald Trump's White House ballroom as a paperweight "after we all blow it up." "In about 10 to 15 years, we are all going to be sitting here with smiles on our faces," Krasner said, according to video footage obtained by WCAU. "And I'm going to have a paperweight sitting on my desk. And do you know what that paper weight's going to be? It's going to be a piece of the ballroom after we blow it up." Krasner, who has previously called Trump a fascist and said he would hunt down Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers, made the comments while speaking at George Washington's historic home in Philadelphia during the city's annual slavery commiseration, according to WCAU. DEM JUSTICES SLAP SOROS-BACKED PHILLY DA WITH POWER STRIP IN STUNNING DECISION: 'NOT RELIABLE' Krasner first called Trump "a pain in the a–," to which an audience member responded, "No, he's the devil!" Krasner then responded, "He's the devil, alright, well there is some evidence to that effect." "The man himself is the embodiment of hate. He is the embodiment of ignorance. He is the embodiment of depriving people of their vote and their education. That's who he is," Krasner continued. TRUMP ORDERS SIGNS OUTSIDE SMITHSONIAN MUSEUM AMID ROW OVER ITS DEPICTION OF AMERICAN HISTORY Krasner was specifically bashing Trump for deciding to replace a slavery exhibit at the Washington home under a March executive order titled, "Restoring Truth and Sanity to American History." Under the order, the National Park Service replaced the panels dedicated to showcasing the history of George Washington's slaves with more broad displays of U.S. history. A protracted legal battle between the city and the Trump administration most recently saw a federal appeals court side with the federal government and rule that Philadelphia had no legal right to dictate the content of the displays at the federally owned site. JUDGE BLOCKS PHILADELPHIA LAW TARGETING MASKED FEDERAL OFFICERS Despite the city's loss to the federal government in the legal fight, Krasner remained defiant. "This memorial will be here, the educational content will be here," Krasner railed Tuesday. "People will be coming to see it, not for a year or two, or not even 20 years. They will be coming to see it as long as this federal park is here." EXCLUSIVE: KENNEDY CENTER BOARD MOVES TO NAME GROUNDS ‘PRESIDENT DONALD J TRUMP PLAZA' "But let me tell you what will not be here," he continued. "There will not be a ballroom. There will not be a Kennedy Center renamed for a fool," Krasner said. Krasner did specify that the envisioned demolition would be "in an official ceremony, just to be clear, in an official ceremony we're gonna blow it up and we're gonna give the taxpayers their money back by selling old pieces as paperweights, and I'm gonna have one on my desk." WHITE HOUSE SEIZES ON DELAYED OBAMA PRESIDENTIAL CENTER OPENING TO CROWN TRUMP ‘BUILDER-IN-CHIEF’ The White House fired back at Krasner's comments about the ballroom project. "President Trump continues to implement long-overdue and necessary renovations to beautify the People’s House as we approach our great Nation’s 250th anniversary of independence. Thanks to the Builder-in-Chief, the White House will be properly glorified and remain in excellent condition for generations to come. Only people who suffer from a severe and incurable disease known as Trump Derangement Syndrome would find a problem with that," White House spokesperson Davis Ingle said in a statement to Fox News Digital. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP When reached by Fox News Digital, U.S. Secret Service's Lead Public Affairs Specialist Nate Herring said, "The U.S. Secret Service investigates anything that can be perceived as a threat toward our protectees. Out of concern for operational security, we do not discuss matters of protective intelligence." Fox News Digital contacted Philadelphia's Justice Department for further comment.

articles.title: Federal judge lifts nationwide block on mail-in voting restrictions
articles.summary: A federal judge in Boston on Wednesday lifted a nationwide block on mail-in voting restrictions, temporarily clearing the way for the Trump administration to begin implementing them ahead of the November midterms. U.S. District Judge Indira Talwani granted the Justice Department’s request to reconsider her earlier injunction in the wake of a Supreme Court ruling…
articles.body:
A federal judge in Boston on Wednesday lifted a nationwide block on mail-in voting restrictions, temporarily clearing the way for the Trump administration to begin implementing them ahead of the November midterms.

U.S. District Judge Indira Talwani granted the Justice Department’s request to reconsider her earlier injunction in the wake of a Supreme Court ruling that found a separate lawsuit challenging President Trump’s order was premature.

“In sum, the court finds that, in light of the Supreme Court’s decision in Trump v. California, Plaintiff Organizations are not likely to prevail as to ripeness without amending their complaint to reflect the fact that a Final Rule has now issued,” Talwani wrote in a nine-page order .

The case was brought by the League of Women Voters and other voting rights groups, who are expected to file a supplemental complaint now that the Postal Service has finalized its rule.

images.caption: The United States Postal Service logo is seen on a mailbox outside a post office in Los Angeles, California, August 17, 2020. (Photo by ROBYN BECK/AFP via Getty Images)
